summary: The reference follows rules 2-7 correctly for every scenario shape its generator produces. Its rule-1 clock correction only works when the host clock ran slow and was stepped forward. A host clock that ran fast, which the direction-neutral contract permits, is left uncorrected, so every pre-step time in the report comes out N seconds late.

unread_or_truncated_ranges: environment/app/evidence/case-1/var/log/auth.log.2.gz, auth.log.3.gz, wtmp, btmp: gzip/binary, read-only tool cannot decode. Treated as opaque. Their byte layout was verified instead from the writer in solution/model.py:491-501 and the reader in solution/triage.py:43-54,81-88. The reference logic was judged from code, so this gap does not block the axis judgement.

findings.claim: Rule 1 correction handles only a host clock that was behind true time and then stepped forward. For a host clock that was ahead and then set right, the reference applies no correction. The guide and instruction never say which way the clock was wrong. The reference then reports every pre-step host-clock time (initial access, failures, sudo, logins/logouts, history stamps, ctimes, dpkg) N seconds late.

finding_evidence.expected_behavior: case-guide.md:9-14 says the host clock 'may have been wrong by a fixed amount for part of the evidence period and then set right, at most once' and 'Report true times, not what the host clock said'. instruction.md:5 allows 'one clock step of 30 to 7,200 seconds' and gives no direction. For a host clock that was N seconds fast before the step, every pre-step host-clock reading must be reported as reading - N.
finding_evidence.actual_behavior: Each pre-step sshd line gives d = true - host = -N < 0. The guard `if d > 0` never fires, so step_n = 0, lag stays False and step_t stays None. fix() then returns every time unchanged, so every pre-step time is reported N seconds late. Even with the sign guard removed, `fix` would still misclassify pre-step readings. The t < step_t test in triage.py:129-130 assumes that pre-step readings lie below the step point, and for a fast clock they reach up to tc+N.
finding_evidence.trace_or_receipt: Static trace, not executed. Take a fast host clock with N = 600 and the step at true time tc = T_ia + 3600. The attacker's Accepted line at true T_ia is logged locally at T_ia + 600, and the collector (record-formats.md:22-27) stamps it T_ia. At triage.py:121-127, d = -600, so neither branch fires and step_t stays None. triage.py:129-130: fix(t) = t. wtmp login record tv_sec = T_ia + 600 → sessions start = T_ia + 600 (triage.py:134,138-142) → initial_access.time = iso(T_ia + 600) (triage.py:251) instead of iso(T_ia). The same shift reaches first_activity via btmp failures (triage.py:135,241), privilege_escalation via the sudo line (triage.py:147-153,192-194) and the persistence windows via ctimes (triage.py:207-235). A persistence ctime near a session boundary can therefore also enter or leave the window. solution/model.py:412-413 (`rec(t) = t - N`) shows the generator only ever produces slow clocks, which is why the reference and generator agree.

findings.reachable_case_or_path: Any evidence directory whose host clock ran N seconds (30..7200) ahead of true time and was then set right after the initial access. The contract describes such a directory as 'wrong by a fixed amount ... then set right' with a '30 to 7,200 seconds' step. Path: triage.py:120-132 → fix() → wtmp/btmp/auth/history/fs-listing/dpkg times.
findings.graded_effect: On such a directory the reference emits wrong initial_access.time, privilege_escalation, first_activity and last_activity (when pre-step), and possibly wrong persistence membership. Each is a field-by-field mismatch. The sealed corpus comes from model.py, which only renders slow clocks, so the current goldens do not exercise this case. The defect is latent: the reference passes its own tests but does not implement the direction-neutral contract the instruction promises for 'many other evidence directories'.
findings.root_invariant: Every host-clock reading on the pre-step side must be corrected by the signed offset that the collector reveals, whichever way the clock was wrong. The pre-step/post-step split must come from the collector's bracketing, not from a slow-clock-only threshold.
implementation_sites: solution/triage.py:120-127 (step detection: d > 0 guard, step_t = first d == 0 line)
solution/triage.py:129-130 (fix: t + step_n when t < step_t)
solution/model.py:373-380 (within_limits: guarantees are argued for the slow-clock case only)
sibling_variants: The same single-direction assumption affects every consumer of fix(): wtmp sessions (triage.py:134), btmp hostile windows (triage.py:135,155-162), dpkg install times for the 2-second package exclusion (triage.py:219), fs-listing ctimes for persistence (triage.py:231), and history stamps (triage.py:249).
interaction_variants: Rule 1 x rule 6: an uncorrected ctime shifted by +N can move a persistence file across an intruder session boundary. The 2-second dpkg comparison stays self-consistent because both sides use the same host clock.

Rule 1 x rule 2: all failures shift by the same amount, so hostile-address detection is unaffected unless the step falls inside a burst, which the reference never corrects in either direction for fast clocks.
findings.minimal_repair_boundary: Either (a) generalise rule-1 handling in solution/triage.py: take the signed offset from collector matches, split pre-step from post-step by the bracketing collector lines rather than `t < step_t`, and add fast-clock scenarios to model.py and the sealed corpus; or (b) narrow the contract (case-guide rule 1 and instruction.md) to say the host clock was behind and was stepped forward, so the reference's slow-clock handling is the whole contract.
closure_evidence: A fast-clock scenario (e.g. N = 600, step after the initial access) where the reference reports initial_access.time equal to the collector's Accepted timestamp
Or: a contract diff stating the step direction, with the existing slow-clock goldens unchanged

checks_performed: Read the instruction, all three /app/docs contracts, the stub, the Dockerfile, and all readable case-1 evidence.
Traced solution/triage.py rule by rule against case-guide.md rules 1-7 and the report.md schema.
Read the generator (solution/model.py build/write_evidence/truth/within_limits) and seal.py to see which scenario shapes the reference must handle.

Traced rule-1 step detection for a slow clock: pre-step readings are below tc-N and the post-step line at tc gives step_t = tc, so the correction is exact. Repeated the trace for a fast clock and found the defect CRS-1.
Traced year inference across Dec→Jan with the last-line vs collected_utc local comparison and the backward month-decrease walk (triage.py:57-78).
Traced wtmp login/logout pairing by tty against the model's tty allocation (a tty is never reused while busy), including an open session with no logout.

Traced the rule-2 hostile window: sliding window of five with ts[i+4]-ts[i] <= 600 includes exactly 600. Checked against the model's attacker burst (exactly 600 s) and the carol/ivan decoy (at least 601 s).

Traced the rule-4 fixed point: address-tied sessions, key fingerprints from intruder-account histories matching Accepted publickey fingerprints, terminal-tied sudo lines, and root added on escalation. Checked the shared-password decoy (victim account from O2) and the admin key in tpham's history.
Traced rule 5 (first root sudo on an intruder tty, or a root login) and the concurrent legitimate sudo decoys on other ttys.

Traced the rule-6 persistence path classifier, the in-window ctime test, and the package exclusion abs(ctime - install) <= 2. Checked the ±2 edge, the touch -r forged mtime, the systemd .wants symlinks, and the certbot-renew decoy between sessions.
Traced rule 7 event set (intruder-source btmp, logins/logouts, tied sudo lines, timestamped history in intruder windows, persistence ctimes; collected_utc excluded for open sessions).
Checked the case-1 cross-consistency of dpkg local times with ctimes (apt-listchanges 03:18:57 at -12:00 = 1640791137).

coverage_sweep.category: Trace an ordinary case and each relevant boundary through the reference
coverage_sweep.reason: Traced the ordinary slow-clock intrusion plus these boundaries: exactly 600 s hostile window, 601 s decoy, ±2 s package exclusion, open session, Dec→Jan year rollover, offsets from -12:00 to +14:00, and 1 to 6 rotated files. All are correct for the slow-clock shape. The step-direction boundary fails (CRS-1).

coverage_sweep.category: Output bytes: widths, precision, formats, paths
coverage_sweep.reason: iso() emits YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ in UTC. The report has exactly the seven keys from report.md, set fields are deduplicated via set/dict and sorted, and privilege_escalation is null when absent. solve.sh installs to /app/triage.py.

coverage_sweep.category: Every branch that updates state (fixed-point loop, session open/close, step state)
coverage_sweep.reason: The fixed-point loop recomputes pe, accounts, keys and addresses until nothing changes. wtmp open_by_line pops on logout. The step state (step_n, lag, step_t) is correct only for a positive offset.
The task is a batch read-only analyzer with no recovery or durability promises.

coverage_sweep.category: Environment/runtime constraints (stdlib only, no /app/evidence dependency, unprivileged read-only)
coverage_sweep.reason: Imports are stdlib only. The script reads only the argv evidence directory, never /app/evidence, and never writes into the evidence.

interaction_sweep.case_or_path: dpkg install inside an intruder window, with its file ctimes at ±2 and a clock step. Both the dpkg time and the ctime go through fix() on the same host clock, so the difference is preserved and the files are excluded.
Fast host clock stepped back: the d < 0 branch is ignored and no correction is applied.

The legitimate user of the victim account logs in from O2 during S1 and runs sudo on another pts. session_at() maps the tty to a non-intruder session, so the sudo is excluded from pe and activity, and O2 is never added to sources.

The key echoed into ~/.ssh/authorized_keys in the victim's history produces a fingerprint. That fingerprint matches the Accepted publickey line from the second address, which is added to sources, and a root key login adds root and sets pe. The admin's key is in the admin's history, and the admin is never an intruder account, so it ties nothing.
The certbot-renew decoy ctime lies between S1 end and S2 start. After the pre-step correction it falls outside every intruder window and is excluded.
